body: @gchanan No, I think that's a different issue. The mentioned issue is related to nn.Conv2d gradient calculate behavior (which depends on CPU backward kernel), and this issue is about manual computation of gradient in nn.grad.

These are for the "slow" backward formulas we have at https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/b71215a9097cbd0170e07db6f89ea9fdd932c4a5/torch/nn/grad.py#L170. @lemonbuffer20 what is your use case for using those formulas as opposed to using autograd to compute gradients?

@zou3519 I was trying to modify convolution backward, specificially, changing batch-wise aggregation (usually sum). Common nn.Conv2d or cudnn_backward does not support such figure, so I tried to implement custom function with nn.grad.conv2d_backward,

Can confirm this is true, and wasted 2 hours on it. The initial repeat is wrong, as it's also repeating the groups. When I change it to only repeat cin, it works.

See my fix in my neural network library here: https://github.com/geohot/tinygrad/commit/8864b373338886a9173d3f823154815535104f28
@nikitaved could you have a look at this one?
I'll look into rewriting the back of these APIs to use the general `convolution_backward` op now that it exists. That should remove any discrepancies and fix this bug.

issue.title: Simplify torch.nn.grad by calling into aten::convolution_backward

repository.name: pytorch
repository.description: Tensors and Dynamic neural networks in Python with strong GPU acceleration

issue.body:
`torch.nn.grad` has its own implementations of gradients for conv1d, conv2d, and conv3d. This PR simplifies them by calling into the unified `aten::convolution_backward` backend instead.

The existing implementation of conv2d_weight is incorrect for some inputs (see issue #51430). This PR fixes the issue.

This PR expands coverage in test_nn to include conv1d_weight, conv2d_weight, and conv3d_weight, which were previously untested. It also expands the cases for conv2d to cover issue #51430.

Fixes #51430
